author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Everyone knows that if a man is rich and single, he must be looking for a wife. It is something society just assumes to be true about wealthy bachelors.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: When a rich man moves into a new area, the people living there immediately think of him as a potential husband for one of their daughters, even if they know nothing about what he actually wants.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: One day, Mrs. Bennet excitedly asked her husband if he had heard the news that Netherfield Park had finally been rented out to someone.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Mr. Bennet calmly told his wife that he had not heard anything about it.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Mrs. Bennet insisted that it was true because she had just spoken to Mrs. Long, who told her all the details about the new renter.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Mr. Bennet chose not to respond to her statement at all.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Frustrated by his silence, Mrs. Bennet loudly asked him if he wanted to know who had actually rented the property.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Mr. Bennet said that he would listen to her if she really wanted to tell him the news.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: This small amount of encouragement was all Mrs. Bennet needed to continue.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: She explained that a wealthy young man named Bingley from northern England was renting it. He had come down earlier in the week in a large carriage to look at the place and agreed to rent it immediately.
